chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Webb's battles with Goodman, Casa Loma and Duke
summary: McRae thinks the Goodman battle was overblown; Webb outplayed Casa Loma with "Hold That Tiger" and respected Duke's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I want to get back to just

one more thing before we leave like the big bands, like the battles of music.
The one we had with Duke Ellington and Chick Webb at the Savoy on Sunday night, I think this was the most outstanding battle of music, much better than the Benny Goodman battle.
I think the Benny Goodman thing was just a thing blown out of proportion. Two bands blowing.
I think everybody knew that Benny didn't have the type of band that Chick Webb had. I knew that and I think everybody else knew that.
Benny had a good band, because -- See, at that time that Chick was blowing everybody out of the -- everybody came up to the Savoy.
Chick was blowing out the Casa Loma, everybody would come there, you know.

I remember one time Glen Gray (inaudible) was playing the Paramount Theater, and they sent a wire to Chick -- sent us a wire. Say when you hear us come up -- see us come up the stairs, play something to

get us in the mood.
And we played something. And when they came in and got up on the bandstand and Chick did play something to get them in the mood, he played a head arrangement on Hold That Tiger.
No music. It was a head arrangement. It was the whole band and Chick had put that thing together.
I'll never forget (inaudible). They stood up and they shouted (inaudible) band excited -- Casa Loma (inaudible) band, so they asked us to play it over again, and we had to play it over again for them, you know.
So, we had things in the band that could stop any bid band, up there against us because (inaudible) like "King Porter's Stomp," "Royal Garden Blues", you know. "Naughty Waltz"-- things like Chick used to do (inaudible).
But the night of the battle of the Duke, we knew Duke had a band. Everybody in the country knew Duke had one of the finest bands.
And he could also change colors -- what we call "changing colors" too, fast as Chick could
